videos.script: A long reply takes seconds. Streaming does not make it faster. It shows the first word sooner. {{wait}} In this lesson you measure that, then read a stream as it crosses the wire, event by event. {{events}} You carry it to a browser through a relay of your own, because the key must never reach the page. {{relay}} Then the two ways a stream ends early. A person presses Stop, and your code closes the connection. Or the provider fails halfway, and the page has half an answer to deal with honestly. {{errors}} Last, what a person sees while the words arrive. Half-written Markdown. A tool call that does not parse yet. And a screen reader that should hear sentences, not fragments. The replies in this lesson were written by the course. The streams, the relay and the errors are real.
